clauses.scope_note: Online-order agreement §7(3): customer remains responsible for monitoring its account balance and replenishing it according to its operating plan. The referenced website reminder-service details are not supplied.
clauses.condition_explanation: The duty applies to the customer as account user and manager; it is not displaced by the provider's balance-insufficient reminder service.

obligation_items.content: Timely check the account balance and replenish it according to the customer’s operating plan.
obligation_items.object: Customer’s Baidu Smart Cloud account balance
obligation_items.trigger: While using the service and managing the account balance.

coverage_notes: The referenced website terms for balance reminders, payment methods, invoice applications, and product-specific rules are not supplied; no contents are inferred.

Payment of provider fees, invoice applications, contractual remedies, contract termination, and general continued-performance duties do not map faithfully to the allowed activities. No Charge clause is used to represent customer payment.

paragraph_audit.reason: Section 4(15) is a company sanctions-status representation at signing, not a permission or prohibition concerning an available activity; no activity rule is created.
Section 4(19) grants Baidu a conditional right to terminate the contract if an export-control policy change makes performance impossible. Contract termination is not an available activity.

Section 7(3) requires the account user and manager to timely check the balance and replenish it according to the operating plan. The referenced reminder-service details are external and not inferred; the provider-payment action itself is not represented.

Section 7(6) describes customer recharge and lists payment channels, while referring to website rules not supplied. Payment to the provider and recharge are not represented by an allowed activity; no external payment rules are inferred.

Section 7(7) describes an optional customer invoice application and refers to website requirements and procedures not supplied. Applying for or issuing an invoice is outside the available activities; no external requirements are inferred.

Section 7(8) describes an optional automatic-renewal setting and automatic fee deduction at the then-current price. Setting automatic renewal and paying the provider are not available activities; Charge would misstate the customer’s payment as third-party charging.

Section 10(1) establishes a breach-and-cure procedure: after a cure notice, failure to effectively cure within 10 days, or an incurable breach that harms the other party or prevents continued cooperation, triggers damages liability. Cure and contract-remedy actions do not fit the available activities.

Section 10(3) states reciprocal delay-compensation and late-payment remedies, including 0.5‰ per day, a 30-day threshold, a 10% amount, continued payment for delivered project results, and an exception for customer-caused delay. Payment of the provider and damages remedies do not fit the available activities.

Section 11(3) requires both parties to continue performing after force majeure or an accidental event ends, when both can perform and continuation is necessary. It does not identify a specific available activity and object to which the general duty can faithfully attach.
Section 12(1)(2) grants Baidu a right to terminate service for the customer’s serious breach, including serious payment, legal, or promise breaches. Termination is not an available activity.
